name: agent-project-kit
purpose: Agent Project Kit: a portable starter kit that installs AI-agent instruction files and project-local .ai templates. New installs use .ai/agent-project-kit; computing-environment remains a legacy name/path for migration only.

machines.primary-heavy: Optional project-defined role for full builds, expensive tests, GPU/data-heavy runs
machines.portable-laptop: Optional project-defined role for edit/review/smoke tasks
machines.remote-server: Optional project-defined role for deployment, services, or batch jobs

added_from_old_package: selected utility scripts and document templates
release_notes: Canonicalized aggregate checksum ordering by relative path so the same shared artifact verifies on WSL/Linux and native Windows.
Separated the synced immutable package root from machine-local launcher and configuration state.
Added project binding schema v2, schema-v1 compatibility, guarded rollback, and multi-machine/self-host safety tests.
Added a Thai DOCX language finalizer with text-preserving Thai/Latin run metadata and downstream installation coverage.
Added a persisted 14-day manifest-only update notice that reports availability without cloning or installing.
Pinned an aggregate package SHA-256 in each shared-runtime project binding and added tamper rejection, real snapshot rollback, and root non-recursion acceptance tests.
Added an opt-in, version-pinned shared-runtime canary with immutable side-by-side installs, explicit resolution failures, isolated tests, and no change to the default per-project snapshot installer.
Completed a route audit across all 47 discovered OneDrive project-state markers: 27 configured projects were reviewed and 20 placeholders were intentionally excluded from routing.
Hardened routing for seminars, course decks, IOI/POSN governance, research supervision, correspondence, nominations, academic-rank operations, and negative mentions of code/tests.
Hardened English routing after six real-project trials: ASCII matching now respects word boundaries and explicit output formats outrank subject-matter terms.

Introduced a v7-compatible structured configuration layer with four-axis request routing, declarative policies/workflows, compact context compilation, token estimates, and non-destructive JSON project state alongside Markdown compatibility files.
Added a machine-validated prompt catalog with eight primary routes, reusable secondary workflows, one-time prompts, legacy redirects, cadence, triggers, and strict composition limits.
Separated Presentation from Course Material Development, converted the old policy prompt to a redirect, and reduced machine discovery to a conditional one-time workflow.
Added Software Development and Automation plus Administrative and Professional Operations as primary routes, made web development a subtype, and added Strategy and Advisory as a secondary workflow.
Extended doctor checks to identify placeholder and stale project state instead of treating every existing PROJECT_STATE file as resumable.
Added Educational Policy Development as a distinct primary route, with Research Activities used as a secondary evidence workflow when appropriate.
Changed the primary task router to six real work types: web development, research activities, content analysis, data analytics, presentation, and course material development.
Added a task router and three-file fast startup contract so agents load only the prompt and state needed for the current request.
Added run-once execution state, a read-only doctor, repeat-install log suppression, and automated fast-start acceptance tests.
Simplified public README files into a lighter install-and-test introduction.
Removed deeper workflow explanations from the README landing pages.
Reduced manifest purpose wording to a public starter-kit description.
Trimmed public README pages while keeping package logic unchanged.
Clarified hierarchical resume prompts so known parent context can be reused while child projects keep sharper local state.
Clarified that L1/L2/L3 loop diagnosis is project-local and should be evaluated at the current hierarchy level before using parent context.
Added status/deadline dashboard guidance so project resumes summarize the last session and next actions by priority and due date.
Added startup version reporting and periodic update-check guidance for installed Agent Project Kit snapshots.
Added a changelog and concise README benefit statements.
Added an existing-project update guide with dry-run, verification, schema decision, and rollback steps.
Added dry-run support to install-from-git scripts so projects can preview package and schema changes before updating.

Added research-project prompt pack for deep dives, literature reviews, counter-argument checks, source credibility, competitive intelligence, trend scans, data interpretation, expert breakdowns, and research briefs.
Added GitHub Pages manifest update checks that refresh package concepts through the existing preserve-state installer.
Added first-install conflict guards so existing user files or directories with Agent Project Kit names are not overwritten unless they already look like kit-managed files.
Changed the canonical installed snapshot path from .ai/computing-environment to .ai/agent-project-kit while keeping computing-environment as a legacy migration path.
Added a GitHub Pages landing page that explains install paths, update checks, safety rules, and where project prompt packs should live.
Refreshed the English and Thai README files so they explain current paths, prompt-pack ownership, and first-install safety rules.
